paper: Sato et al. 2021, Variational quantum algorithm based on the minimum potential energy for solving the Poisson equation (Phys. Rev. A 104, 052409; arXiv:2106.09333)

questions.q: How much of the O(1)-vs-O(n) per-cost-evaluation measurement advantage of Sato 2021 over Liu 2020 survives once total shots-to-target-error are budgeted end-to-end (i.e., accounting for the increased iteration count and per-iteration variance of the potential-energy cost)?
questions.basis: REPORT.md Claim C5 verifies T_C = 4 constant-cost terms (Dirichlet) for Sato vs O(n) for Liu by inspection of Eq. (14), and C6 reports T_it ~ n^2.6 (Sato) vs ~n^4.2 (Liu) — but was not tested in this pass. The paper's headline advantage is a product of these two factors and is asserted, not benchmarked end-to-end at fixed target trace distance.
next_steps: Implement both Sato Eq. (14) cost and the Liu-2020 VQA-linear-solver cost in the same NumPy statevector harness.
Add a finite-shot sampler (multinomial over |psi|^2) with a variable shots-per-eval knob to both.
For n in {3, 4, 5, 6}, at target eps_tr = 0.01, sweep shots per eval and count total shots to convergence (mean over 20 seeds).
Report total-shots(n) log-log fit for Sato vs Liu; the crossover-n (if any) is the honest quantum-advantage boundary.

questions.q: Does the minimum-potential-energy VQA extend to the variable-coefficient Poisson equation -div(a(x) grad u) = f (a(x) > 0) and to 2D/3D Poisson with retained O(1) measurement cost, or does the T_C constant blow up with the number of nonzero stencil bands?
questions.basis: REPORT.md Sec. 1 and C5 both restrict tested scope to the 1D constant-coefficient Poisson operator A = tridiag[-1, 2, -1] with Dirichlet/periodic/Neumann BCs. The paper's O(1) measurement claim depends on A having a fixed, small number of Pauli-string terms in its decomposition, which is a property of 1D constant-coefficient discretization and is not obviously preserved for variable-coefficient or higher-dimensional Laplacians.
next_steps: Enumerate the Pauli decomposition of the 2D Dirichlet 5-point Laplacian on a 2^n x 2^n grid; count T_C.
Repeat for the variable-coefficient 1D operator with a(x) discretized on the grid; count T_C as a function of a(x)'s spectral bandwidth.
Extend vqa_poisson_replicate.py to the 2D case, rerun the n=4 (16x16 grid = 8 qubits total) trace-distance experiment, and record actual per-iter cost queries.
Report scaling of T_C with dimension and coefficient variation; flag any regime where T_C is no longer O(1).

questions.q: At what point does the hardware-efficient Ry+CNOT-ladder ansatz depth L exhaust the expressibility-vs-trainability trade-off for larger n — i.e., where does over-parameterization (as observed here at n<=4 with L=5) give way to barren-plateau-limited trainability, and does the minimum-potential-energy cost inherit or attenuate the standard local/global cost barren-plateau behavior?
questions.basis: REPORT.md Sec. 4.1 explicitly notes n=2..4 results are near machine precision because L=5 is over-parameterized for those small dimensions, and n=5 mean trace distance jumps to 0.0070. Convergence iteration counts jump from ~8 (n=2) to ~440 (n=5), suggesting the landscape is already stiffening. The paper reports up to n=5 only; no data on where trainability fails.
next_steps: For n in {5, 6, 7, 8} and L in {3, 5, 7, 10}, sample 200 random parameter points and compute Var[dE_h/dtheta_j] — an empirical barren-plateau curve for Sato's cost.
Do the same for the standard global-observable VQE cost as a baseline; report the ratio.
For each (n, L), run 20 random-init L-BFGS-B trials to a fixed budget and report success rate at eps_tr <= 0.01. Locate the trainability cliff.
Compare against theoretical barren-plateau predictions (McClean 2018 / Cerezo 2021) parametrized for this cost.

questions.q: Does the ~2.5% quantum-norm underestimation observed both by Sato 2021 and by this replication survive on real NISQ hardware, and can it be distinguished from shot noise + gate noise + readout error contributions?
questions.basis: REPORT.md Sec. 4.2 confirms the paper's Fig. 3(b) underestimation direction and magnitude (quantum 24.66 vs classical 25.30 at n=5, Dirichlet), but under noiseless NumPy statevector simulation only. The replication's own critique section flags this as an expressibility artifact, not a NISQ effect. The paper argues the method is NISQ-friendly, but this replication provides no evidence for that claim.
next_steps: Add a Qiskit-Aer noiseless-shot backend and reproduce the n=5 Dirichlet result at 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 shots per cost eval; report the noise-floor curve for the norm.
Add a depolarizing + readout-error noise model calibrated to a current IBM Quantum device (ibm_kyoto or ibm_osaka) and repeat.
If access is available, run n=3 on real IBM hardware (~30 CNOTs, plausible), otherwise stop at the calibrated simulator.
Decompose the observed norm error into expressibility (statevector residual), shot noise, and gate/readout noise; report each contribution.

questions.q: How does Sato 2021 compare against contemporaneous VQLS (Bravo-Prieto et al. 2019/2020) and against HHL (as an asymptotic-only reference) for the same Poisson operator, in terms of both total quantum resources to reach eps_tr = 0.01 and end-to-end wall time on a statevector simulator?
questions.basis: REPORT.md Sec. 1 and the paper itself only benchmark against the prior Liu et al. 2020/2021 VQA-linear-solver approach. The critique section (REPORT.md Sec. Genuine Critique) explicitly flags that no comparison was made against VQLS or HHL. Sato's central claim is measurement-efficiency; VQLS uses a different (Hadamard-test-based) cost that is also amenable to Poisson.
next_steps: Implement VQLS (with the local Hadamard-test cost of Bravo-Prieto 2020) for the same Poisson operator in the same NumPy harness, sharing the ansatz and optimizer.
Run head-to-head at n in {3, 4, 5} for Dirichlet BC: log per-iter cost queries, total iterations to eps_tr=0.01, and wall time (all noiseless).

For HHL, compute only the asymptotic query complexity for the tridiagonal Poisson operator (kappa(A) ~ N^2 = 4^n) and tabulate alongside the empirical VQA curves — do NOT try to simulate HHL end-to-end at n>=4.
Publish a resource-comparison table Sato/Liu/VQLS/HHL for the same problem; state clearly where the crossovers are.
